eyebrow: Ethical Hacking, Pentesting & Purple Team · Chapter 3
subtitle: Lesson 9 · Scanning and Enumeration

steps.label: SYN/ACK returns
steps.sub: port is open — Nmap replies RST, never finishes the handshake

steps.label: RST returns
steps.sub: port is closed — nothing listening there

steps.label: No reply at all
steps.sub: filtered — a firewall likely dropped the probe, unknown either way

code:
nmap -sS 10.10.10.5

PORT     STATE    SERVICE
22/tcp   open     ssh
80/tcp   open     http
443/tcp  open     https
3389/tcp filtered ms-wbt-server
caption: -sS is a half-open scan: it never completes the three-way handshake.

code:
# No raw-socket privileges? Fall back to a full connect scan:
nmap -sT 10.10.10.5

# UDP needs real time budgeted, not a blind full-range scan:
nmap -sU --top-ports 100 10.10.10.5
caption: -sT completes the handshake via the OS socket API; -sU is slow and often ambiguous.

steps.label: -T0 / -T1
steps.sub: paranoid/sneaky — slow, far less likely to trip IDS thresholds

steps.label: -T4 / -T5
steps.sub: aggressive/insane — fast, but an easily detected traffic burst
